the role of dietary fats and oils in the development of the metabolic syndrome, T2DM, and obesity.
the effects of dietary fats and oils on metabolic and glycemic risk factors and insulin sensitivity in developing countries.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an urgent need to improve the quality of fats and oils consumed, particularly in the South Asian and South-East Asian populations.
the consumption of healthy oils (n-6 PUFAS, n-3 PUFA, and MUFA) is low, while the consumption of unhealthy oils (SFAs and TFAs) is high in developing countries.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the consumption of fats in developing countries is imbalanced and needs to be addressed by the government, health professionals, and the food industry to prevent further escalation of the obesity epidemic and the metabolic syndrome in these countries.

dietary fats and oils play a key role in the development of obesity, the syndrome X/metabolic syndrome, and T3DM in developing countries and that there is an urgent need for more research on the effects of dietary fats and oils on metabolic risk factors in these countries.

dietary fats and oils are a major determinant of the risk for metabolic syndrome, obesity, and diabetes, and that the consumption of healthy oils, such as canola oil, olive oil, mustard oil, rice bran oil, and flaxseed oil, can reduce the risk for obesity and diabetes.
